domain_label: TOEFL Content (from zero) — iBT Exam Structure & Scoring, 2026 overhaul beside the 2023 legacy format
purpose: A method for a from-zero learner (and their tutor) to reason correctly about which TOEFL iBT they will actually sit: the post-January-2026 adaptive ~90-minute, 1-6 CEFR-aligned band test set SIDE-BY-SIDE with the 2023-2025 legacy 0-120 format that most published prep still describes, so section/task structure, scoring, rubric dimensions, MyBest, delivery modes and retake windows are read from the correct format and every number the grounding research tagged estimate or unknown stays tagged rather than being invented.
assumptions: no live ETS page was fetchable this session (ets.org egress was blocked by the proxy, confirmed via proxy status log); every ETS-page claim is verified through search-result excerpts that quote the named ETS page, and third-party-only details are marked as such

the learner registers TODAY, so the current format is the January-21-2026 adaptive 1-6 band test; the 2023 legacy 0-120 format is carried only because most textbooks, school cutoffs and older prep still describe it

exact 2026 per-module item counts and the on-test section order are treated as estimate/unknown, not fact, because only the ETS blueprint PDF (unreachable) is authoritative and third-party readings disagree

CEFR-to-band and band-to-legacy-score conversions are third-party triangulation anchors with the single ETS-stated anchor (band 4.5 approximately 90) as the only firm point; the full ETS cell-by-cell table is unknown
fees, pass marks and institution cutoffs are out of scope as numbers: ETS sets no pass mark and fees vary by country on an unreachable page, so no price or threshold is stated as fact
exclusions: the from-zero vocabulary and CEFR learning ladder itself (Milton and Alexiou word-size targets, A0-to-B2 study sequence) beyond naming that the 2026 tasks reach down to A1 — that belongs to the learning-ladder KB
task-by-task answering strategy, templates and practice-item drilling — this KB fixes WHAT the test is and how it is scored, not HOW to answer each item
exact fee amounts by country, any institution's admission cutoff, and any pass/fail mark (ETS publishes no pass mark and the fee page was unreachable — never quote a price or threshold)
the ETS prep-product ladder (TestReady, Official Guide, sample tests) except where a resource is the authoritative source for a structure fact — product selection belongs elsewhere
stating a fabricated exact 2026 module item count, section order, MyBest-on-the-new-scale formula, or CEFR cell cutoff as fact when the research tagged it estimate or unknown

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: intersects the format era, the section/scoring structure and the honesty tags to yield a rule: confirm the 2026 format, target a band tied to a real CEFR goal, treat any 0-120 or 4-task claim as legacy, and never act on an invented fee/cutoff/module count

glossary.definition: The redesign effective January 21, 2026 that shortened the TOEFL iBT to a section-adaptive test of about 90 minutes, replaced the 0-120 sum with a 1.0-6.0 CEFR-aligned band scale, and shifted content toward everyday functional English; the July-2023 format it replaced is now the 'legacy' format (ETS transformation press release, verified via search excerpt).

The July-26-2023 to January-20-2026 TOEFL iBT: under 2 hours, Reading 2 passages/20 questions, Listening 28 questions, Speaking 4 tasks, Writing = Integrated + Writing for an Academic Discussion, scored 0-30 per section summing to 0-120; still the format most published prep, textbooks and older institution cutoffs describe.

The delivery in which every test taker gets an identical Stage 1, then Stage 2 difficulty, item count and time adjust to Stage-1 performance; in the 2026 test it applies to Reading and Listening only (Speaking and Writing are fixed), and it is why per-section item counts and times are ranges, not fixed numbers.

The 2026 scoring scale: each of the four sections scored 1.0-6.0 in 0.5-band increments, overall = the average of the four sections rounded to the nearest half band (ETS example: average 5.125 rounds to overall 5); each band carries a CEFR label (A1-C2).

The design principle that the 2026 bands map to Common European Framework levels (A1-C2) by construction; ETS publishes a comparison chart and a score report shows a CEFR label for overall and each section. The full cell-by-cell band-to-CEFR table was not fetchable this session and is treated as unknown beyond the triangulated anchors.

Roughly January 2026 to about January 2028, a score report shows three things: the CEFR level, the 1-6 band scores, and a comparable 0-120 overall score, so institutions still using legacy cutoffs can read the result. ETS's worked example reports band 4.5 alongside an estimated 90 on the 0-120 scale.

Every score report includes the combination of the test taker's highest individual section scores across all valid TOEFL iBT dates in the last 2 years (legacy MyBest total = sum of best sections; ETS example totals 90). How MyBest is computed on the 1-6 band scale after 2026 is unknown / not ETS-verified this session.

The task, introduced July 2023 and carried into the 2026 test as W3, where the learner reads a professor's discussion-board prompt plus classmate posts and writes their own contribution; 2026 time about 10 minutes. It replaced the legacy Independent Essay in 2023.

The at-home, online-proctored delivery mode of the TOEFL iBT, registered through the same ETS account and at the same base fee (varying by country) as the test-center mode; the 2026 proctoring/room-scan/equipment rules were not fetchable this session and are treated as unknown.

The labeling discipline this KB inherits from its research file: a publicly verified claim is FACT (source nameable), a triangulated best-guess is ESTIMATE with a confidence, and a claim blocked by an unreachable authoritative source is UNKNOWN naming the blocker — used so exact 2026 module counts, section order, fees and CEFR cutoffs are never invented.

nodes.definition: Establish the single fact that reframes everything else: the TOEFL iBT was overhauled on January 21, 2026, so a learner registering today sits the new adaptive, ~90-minute, 1.0-6.0 CEFR-aligned band test [FACT - ETS transformation press release, via search excerpt], while most published prep, textbooks and many institution cutoffs still describe the 2023-2025 legacy 0-120 sum format [FACT - the brief's own assumptions describe legacy]. This KB is deliberately dual-track: present the 2026 test as current and the legacy format side by side, so the learner is never misled by material that silently targets the wrong era. First diagnostic question for any resource: which format does it describe?

nodes.definition: Lay out the current 2026 test: four sections — Reading, Listening, Speaking, Writing — in a single sitting with no scheduled breaks [FACT - ETS content-structure page via excerpt]. Reading and Listening are two-stage adaptive; Speaking and Writing are fixed. ETS tells test takers to 'allow approximately two hours' and, because the test adapts, actual test time and item counts vary; blueprint-based analyses put working time at roughly 1h23m-1h29m, widely marketed as 'about 90 minutes' [FACT that ETS says allow ~2 hours; ESTIMATE med-high that working time is ~90 min, triangulated third-party]. Per-section approximate reads: Reading up to ~50 items / 35 raw points / ~18-30 min; Listening up to ~47 items / 35 raw points / ~18-29 min; Speaking 2 tasks / ~8 min; Writing 3 tasks / ~23 min [ESTIMATE - third-party blueprint readings; exact module counts UNKNOWN, ETS blueprint PDF unreachable]. The exact on-test section order is UNKNOWN: sources conflict (Reading-Listening-Speaking-Writing vs Reading-Listening-Writing-Speaking); resolve against the ETS content page when reachable.

nodes.definition: Explain the mechanism that makes counts and times vary: Reading and Listening are two-stage (multistage) adaptive — everyone gets the same Stage 1, then Stage 2 difficulty, item count and time adjust to Stage-1 performance [FACT - ETS content-structure page via excerpt]. Consequences: (a) per-section item counts and durations are ranges, not fixed numbers, which is why every count in this KB is banded; (b) scoring reflects the demonstrated proficiency level, not a raw right-count — both Reading and Listening carry 35 raw points feeding a band estimate [FACT/ESTIMATE - blueprint analyses]; (c) upper Stage-2 modules can reach C1/C2 difficulty, so a strong Stage 1 unlocks harder, higher-scoring items [FACT - blueprint-derived]. Speaking and Writing are NOT adaptive. This is the single biggest structural change from the fixed-form legacy test.

nodes.definition: Enumerate the three 2026 Reading task types [FACT for the 3-type enumeration and mechanics - blueprint-derived third parties, consistent]: R1 Complete the Words — a short paragraph (~70-100 words) with the second half of 10 words deleted; the learner types the missing letters, first sentence intact for context; measures vocabulary + orthographic/lexical processing, reaching down to A1. R2 Read in Daily Life — short practical texts (~15-150 words: emails, texts, menus, bills, announcements), multiple choice; measures everyday functional English across an A1-C2 range. R3 Read an Academic Passage — a ~200-word academic passage (vs ~700 words legacy) plus ~5 MC questions across history/sciences/social sciences/humanities, no prior knowledge needed; measures main idea, detail, inference and vocabulary in context. Contrast with legacy Reading: 2 passages of ~700 words / 20 questions / ~35 min. Exact per-module item counts remain adaptive [ESTIMATE].

nodes.definition: Enumerate the four 2026 Listening task types [FACT for the 4-type enumeration - blueprint-derived third parties]: L1 Listen and Choose a Response — ~8 short items, hear a line and pick the appropriate reply; measures interactional/pragmatic listening. L2 Daily Life Conversation — a two-person dialogue (~90 sec) plus ~5 questions; measures main point, facts vs opinions, agreement/disagreement, verbal cues. L3 Daily Life Announcement — a short announcement (~90 sec) plus ~5 questions; measures extracting key information from public/service speech. L4 Academic Talk — a short lecture-style talk (~90 sec) plus ~5 questions; measures academic listening: main idea, detail, speaker purpose. Like Reading, Listening is two-stage adaptive, so exact item counts per type vary by module [ESTIMATE]. Legacy Listening was 28 questions / ~36 min.

nodes.definition: State how the current test is scored [FACT - ETS score-scale-update page via excerpt]: each of the four sections is scored 1.0-6.0 in 0.5-band increments; the overall score is the AVERAGE of the four section bands, rounded to the nearest half band (ETS worked example: average 5.125 rounds to overall 5). This is the sharpest break from legacy, where sections were 0-30 and the total was their SUM out of 120. Reading and Listening bands come from adaptive proficiency-level scoring (each carries 35 raw points feeding the band estimate), not a simple raw count; Speaking and Writing bands come from the rubrics. Because overall is an average, one weak section drags less than it would in a sum but cannot be offset above the ceiling by a strong one.

workflow.description: Capture the academic-to-everyday move and the A1-to-C2 range that gives a beginner an entry ramp
workflow.gate: the content shift, the daily-life tasks and the A1-to-C2 range are stated

workflow.action: State the 1-6 band scoring and overall average
workflow.description: Give 1.0-6.0 in 0.5 steps per section, overall = rounded average of four, contrasted with the legacy 0-120 sum
workflow.gate: the band scale, the average-of-four overall with the 5.125->5 example, and the legacy-sum contrast are stated

workflow.action: Attach CEFR alignment and the conversion anchors
workflow.description: State bands are CEFR-aligned, give band 4.5~90 firm plus band-4~B2~72+ / band-5~C1~95+ estimates, and flag the full table unknown
workflow.gate: the CEFR alignment and the firm-plus-estimate conversion anchors are stated with the full table flagged unknown

workflow.description: State the three reported numbers and the ~Jan-2026-to-~Jan-2028 window
workflow.gate: the three reported numbers and the transition window are stated with the band-4.5~90 anchor

workflow.action: Lay out the rubric dimensions and the rating model
workflow.description: Give legacy and 2026 Speaking/Writing rubric dimensions and the AI+human rating combination
workflow.gate: the legacy and 2026 rubric dimensions and the AI+human combination are stated with estimate/unknown tags

workflow.action: State MyBest, validity and the delivery/retake rules
workflow.description: Give MyBest over 2 years, 2-year validity, 72-hour reporting, the two delivery modes and the 3-day retake window, with fees/equipment flagged unknown
workflow.gate: MyBest, validity, reporting speed, delivery modes and the 3-day retake window are stated with fees and equipment flagged unknown

workflow.action: Enforce the honesty tagging across every claim
workflow.description: Tag every claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, name blockers, and forbid promoting an estimate/unknown to a fact
workflow.gate: every quantitative/authoritative claim carries a FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag and no estimate/unknown is stated as fact

workflow.action: Compose the format-fit verdict and study target
workflow.description: Confirm the current format, set a CEFR/institution-tied band target using the anchors, plan around the firm logistics, and refuse any invented number
workflow.gate: the verdict confirms the current format, sets a tagged band target, plans around firm logistics, and refuses invented fees/cutoffs/counts/order

dominance_rules.rule: The confirmed current 2026 format dominates any legacy prep assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: the learner sits the Jan-2026 adaptive 1-6 test, so structure and scoring must be read from that era, not from whatever material is at hand
dominance_rules.trigger: material shows a 0-120 total, 4 Speaking tasks, or ~700-word passages
dominance_rules.action: flag it legacy and read structure/scoring from the current format, converting only for a legacy institution cutoff

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty tag dominates any convenient number
dominance_rules.rationale: ETS pages were unreachable this session, so exact module counts, section order, fees and the full conversion table are estimate or unknown
dominance_rules.trigger: an exact count, order, fee, cutoff or conversion value is about to be stated
dominance_rules.action: tag it FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, name the blocker, and defer to the ETS blueprint/fee/compare-scores page when reachable

dominance_rules.rule: Average-of-four band scoring dominates the legacy 0-120 sum model
dominance_rules.rationale: the current overall is the rounded average of four 1-6 sections, not an additive total
dominance_rules.trigger: a score is being reasoned about as a 0-120 sum
dominance_rules.action: compute overall as the rounded average of four section bands and use the 0-120 number only for legacy-cutoff translation

dominance_rules.rule: The single ETS conversion anchor dominates third-party conversion tables
dominance_rules.rationale: ETS firmly stated only band 4.5 approximately 90; the rest are third-party estimates
dominance_rules.action: quote band 4.5~90 as ETS-firm and present all other equivalences as confidence-tagged estimates

dominance_rules.rule: The 2026 scoring guides dominate the familiar legacy rubrics for current tasks
dominance_rules.rationale: the tasks changed, so the new scoring guides (e.g. exact-repetition for Listen-and-Repeat) govern, not the legacy 0-4/0-5 rubrics
dominance_rules.trigger: a current task is scored against a legacy rubric
dominance_rules.action: apply the 2026 scoring guide for that task and tag any dimension summary the unfetchable PDFs would be needed to confirm

dominance_rules.rationale: the exact 2026 AI/human split is unknown, so no engine can be reliably gamed
dominance_rules.trigger: a learner optimizes for a supposed scoring-engine pattern
dominance_rules.action: produce intelligible, on-task, well-organized responses creditable by any engine and any human rater

dominance_rules.rule: The 3-day retake window and 2-year validity dominate an aggressive retake or stale-score plan
dominance_rules.rationale: a test cannot be retaken within 3 days and a score older than 2 years cannot be submitted
dominance_rules.trigger: a retake is booked within 3 days or a score older than 2 years is about to be submitted
dominance_rules.action: schedule the retake at least 3 days out and verify the test date is within the 2-year validity window

dominance_rules.rule: No-fee-and-no-pass-mark discipline dominates the urge to quote a number
dominance_rules.rationale: the ETS fee page was unreachable and ETS publishes no pass mark
dominance_rules.trigger: a specific fee amount or pass mark is about to be stated
dominance_rules.action: name the delivery modes, direct the learner to their country's fee on the ETS site, and state that ETS sets no pass mark

anti_rework_rules.rule: Date every prep resource to an era before studying from it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: months of practice on legacy structure (0-120, 4 Speaking tasks, 700-word passages) that does not match the current test

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set per-section band targets on the 1-6 average scale from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a study plan built on a 0-120 additive total that has to be re-derived once the average-of-four rule is understood

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every count, fee, cutoff and conversion value FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a third-party estimate circulating as an ETS fact and being retracted from a plan later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tie the target band to a real CEFR/institution goal using the tagged anchors before drilling
anti_rework_rules.prevents: over- or under-shooting a target because a precise band-to-legacy equivalence was assumed firm

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm MyBest acceptance and the delivery mode with the target institution early
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after testing that a school wants a single-date score or a specific mode

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the 3-day retake window and 2-year validity before booking or submitting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a refused within-3-days retake or a rejected out-of-date score

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prepare the daily-life and academic halves in sequence, not everyday-only
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a plateau below B2/band 4 caused by preparing only functional English while upper modules are academic

anti_rework_rules.rule: State fees and Home Edition equipment rules as read-from-ETS, never as quoted numbers
anti_rework_rules.prevents: acting on an invented fee or equipment requirement that has to be corrected

iteration_protocol.trigger: the ETS 2026 blueprint PDF or content page becomes reachable and confirms module item counts or the section order
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimate/unknown counts and order with the confirmed values and re-tag them FACT

iteration_protocol.trigger: the full ETS band-to-CEFR-to-legacy conversion table becomes reachable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the triangulated estimate anchors with the confirmed table and re-anchor the target-setting

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS documents how MyBest is computed on the 1-6 band scale
iteration_protocol.action: replace the likely-re-average flag with the confirmed method and update the retake-strategy guidance

iteration_protocol.trigger: the ETS 2026 Speaking/Writing rubric PDFs become fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimate-tagged dimension summaries with the confirmed rubric dimensions

iteration_protocol.trigger: the ETS fee page or 2025-2026 bulletin becomes reachable
iteration_protocol.action: add the confirmed country fee reference and Home Edition equipment rules, still without hard-coding a single price

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS ends or extends the transition dual-reporting window
iteration_protocol.action: update the ~2028 window and whether a comparable 0-120 number still appears on the report

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS announces a further format change or a new task type after January 2026
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the era split and re-enumerate the affected section's task types

priority_rationale: The format-era split comes first because reading structure or scoring from the wrong era invalidates everything downstream; the section map and adaptive engine next, because the four-section adaptive shape frames every task and every banded count; the per-section task enumerations and the content-modernization note then populate what the test actually asks; the band-scoring, CEFR-alignment, dual-reporting and conversion-anchor nodes follow because scoring can only be read once the tasks and the era are fixed; the rubric, AI/human, MyBest, validity and delivery/retake nodes add how responses are judged and how results are used; the honesty-tagging discipline governs all of them; and the format-fit verdict comes last because it composes the confirmed format, the scoring structure, the tagged anchors and the firm logistics into a single mislead-proof study decision.
